clue.text: This vehicle cannot be repaired immediately, we're informed

indicators.note: being informed means being told, so the words are heard said aloud rather than seen written

parts.note: right off means at once, immediately

explanation.surface: A garage tells a motorist straight away that their crashed car is beyond saving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we're informed' signals that RIGHT OFF (immediately) is heard, and it sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurer declares a vehicle too damaged to be worth repairing a total loss, a familiar British usage.

clue.text: Page taken from middle of telephone book

indicators.note: taking from the middle means keeping only the central part of the word

parts.note: a telephone directory is the phone book

explanation.surface: A page ripped out of the middle of the phone book.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove DI and RY from the ends of DIRECTORY.
explanation.definitionFit: The right-hand page of an open book is called by this printing term, opposite verso.

clue.text: Much improved, given revolutionary treatment?

definitions.meaning: a failing business or team that has been transformed for the better

explanation.definitionFit: A transformed fortune and a spinning object are both described by this phrase.

clue.text: Exercise diplomacy after ejecting clubs in international competition

indicators.note: exercise suggests working the letters over into a new order

parts.note: C is the card-game abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Use tact after throwing out clubs in an international event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after ejecting' drops C (clubs) from DIPLOMACY; 'Exercise' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Olympic Games, or another international contest such as a chess tournament, are known by this term.

clue.text: Be really eager to go on an ego trip?

definitions.meaning: to be desperately keen to do something

definitions.text: to go on an ego trip?
definitions.meaning: to trip over yourself, read literally

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for overeagerness also literally describes tripping over one's own self.

clue.text: Clear half the street

parts.note: demi- is the prefix meaning half
St is the standard abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: An instruction to clear half the road of traffic or snow.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear mist or condensation from a windscreen is the verb meaning to make it clear.

clue.text: With onset of depression, one has a tranquilliser

indicators.note: onset is the start, so the first letter of the word depression

parts.note: an owner is one who has something

explanation.surface: A depressed patient gets a sedative.
explanation.definitionFit: A depressant drug that calms is called this informally.

clue.text: Stick up for fool

definitions.meaning: to rob someone violently in the street

explanation.definitionFit: Both a street robbery and a gullible dupe go by this short slang word.

clue.text: Capital Radio gives entertainer opening

indicators.note: what radio gives is heard, not read

parts.note: a singer is an entertainer and a pore is a tiny opening

explanation.surface: A London radio station hands a performer a break.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital Radio is a London station, so 'Capital' looks part of the name. It is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The city-state's capital shares its name with the country.

clue.text: Having the bends at sea, originally a problem for many a sailor?

definitions.text: a problem for many a sailor?

indicators.note: originally points to the start of the word sea, its opening letter

parts.note: having bends means curvy, with lots of curves

explanation.surface: A diver's decompression sickness, the bends, is suggested as a hazard for seamen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The bends' is the diving illness, a red herring: here it just means curves.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitamin C deficiency disease was the notorious affliction of sailors on long voyages without fresh fruit.

clue.text: Scottish solicitor left worker without money

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: a worker ant is the crossword's standard worker
a wage is money paid for work

explanation.surface: A Scottish lawyer abandoned an employee who has no money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it is the old sense of outside. Law agent is a Scottish legal title.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland the title for a solicitor qualified to practise in the courts was a legal agent of this name.

clue.text: Nothing to such an affair? On the contrary

definitions.text: Nothing to such an affair? On the contrary

parts.words: Nothing to such an affair? On the contrary
parts.note: the word for nothing in tennis scoring, nil, is also what is added in front of the word affair to name a romance; so it is not nothing to it but the other way round

explanation.surface: A dismissive remark that there was nothing to the affair, promptly contradicted.
explanation.definitionFit: A tennis score of zero is called by this word, and the same word names a romantic affair.

clue.text: Daringly original articles backing power given to Catholic Church

indicators.note: backing means coming behind, so these pieces follow the others

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics
Rome stands for the Roman Catholic Church, as in 'going over to Rome'
the is the definite article
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Bold new writing supporting authority being granted to the Church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' puts the articles THE and AN behind P and ROME.
explanation.definitionFit: Prometheus stole fire for mankind, so the adjective from his name describes daring, creative boldness.

clue.text: Successfully pursuing wife in Cambridgeshire location

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the second

parts.note: Huntingdon is a market town in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: Someone's wife lives in an English town.
explanation.walkthrough: Huntingdon is a market town in Cambridgeshire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracking someone down until caught is to pursue them successfully.

clue.text: A British monarch faces challenge in Welsh town

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword's queen
to dare someone is to challenge them

explanation.surface: A British king or queen meets a confrontation in a Welsh town.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen. Aberdare is a town in the South Wales valleys.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberdare is a former mining town in the Cynon Valley of South Wales.

clue.text: Islander's given wrong number phone endlessly engaged

indicators.note: engaged as gears mesh, one piece set into another
wrong means the letters are in the wrong order
endlessly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: to dial is to phone

explanation.surface: An islander gets a wrong number because the line is engaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' makes BERMUN; 'endlessly' drops the last letter; 'engaged' sets the result inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Bermuda, the Atlantic island territory, is called this.

clue.text: In Cologne, regularly wasted time

indicators.note: letters thrown away at regular intervals, so every other letter of the phrase is kept

explanation.surface: Someone frittered away time on a trip to Cologne.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the odd letters of IN COLOGNE leaves N, O, O, N.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday is a specific time of day, twelve o'clock.

clue.text: Maybe tape tune? Right

parts.note: a measure is an old word for a tune or dance

explanation.surface: Someone checks a tape recording of a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A tape measure is one example of a measuring device, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Wife wrapped in a fur

indicators.note: wrapped suggests the letters are folded up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman is bundled up in a fur coat.
explanation.definitionFit: The German word for a married woman, also used for wife, is a crossword standard.

clue.text: Crack in single track railway at the start

parts.note: one means single
a railway line is a track

indicators.note: at the start points to the opening letter of railway

explanation.surface: A fault appears in a single-track railway line near its beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' looks like a fissure, but it is a joke or wisecrack.
explanation.definitionFit: A wisecrack is a single short witty remark, a quip delivered in one sentence.

clue.text: One stores wood for burning

indicators.note: stores means holds within, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: fir is a softwood

explanation.surface: Someone keeps firewood for the fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Alight or ablaze is the meaning of burning.

clue.text: Peaches smell good, getting eaten by people in restaurant

parts.note: hum is British slang for a bad smell

indicators.note: being eaten by means going inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: diners are people eating in a restaurant

explanation.surface: Ripe fruit that smells nice is being eaten by restaurant customers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peaches' is not fruit but excellent things, as in 'she's a peach'. HUM is slang for a stink.
explanation.definitionFit: A peach is slang for anything outstanding, and a humdinger is likewise a remarkable person or thing.

clue.text: English appreciate retired French writer

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: to dig something is slang for appreciating it

explanation.surface: An Englishman admires a French author who has stopped working.
explanation.definitionFit: Andre Gide was a French novelist and Nobel laureate, author of The Immoralist.

clue.text: No show of hostility in prison officer's shift?

indicators.note: no means the following piece is absent

parts.note: a wardress is a female prison warder
war is the ultimate show of hostility

explanation.surface: A prison guard's change of hours goes off without any aggression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shift' looks like a work period, but it is a loose dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A shift is a simple straight-cut frock, a kind of garment.

clue.text: Chairman's report?

parts.note: an important boss makes a sound, read as the bang of an important person

explanation.surface: The chairman's annual report to shareholders.
explanation.definitionFit: A bigwig or important person is slangily called this, and a report is literally a loud bang.

clue.text: Old boy's first name: Jack

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word name

parts.note: OB is a former pupil, old boy

explanation.surface: An old schoolboy's first name is Jack.
explanation.walkthrough: In cribbage, 'one for his nob' scores for the jack of the turned-up suit.
explanation.definitionFit: In cribbage the jack of the turn-up suit is called by this name.

clue.text: My services are on the house

definitions.text: My services are on the house

parts.words: My services are on the house
parts.note: on the house usually means free, but here the tradesman works literally on top of a house

explanation.surface: A tradesman offering free work.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who builds or repairs roofs works literally on the top of a house.

clue.text: Bus lane designed to avoid double bend proves inadequate

indicators.note: designed means newly arranged, so the letters are laid out afresh

parts.note: the letter S is shaped like a double bend, as in an S-bend

explanation.surface: A bus lane laid out to bypass an S-bend turns out to be inadequate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to avoid' drops S, the double bend, from BUS LANE before 'designed' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Being incapable or lacking the ability is what an inadequate person or thing amounts to.

clue.text: Resolution shown by marines boarding splendid ship

indicators.note: boarding means getting on, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: fine means splendid
RM is the Royal Marines
SS is steamship

explanation.surface: Determination is displayed by marines climbing aboard a fine vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resolution' is determination, not a decision or screen sharpness.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolution as determination is a synonym of steadiness of purpose.
